summary: rogue3#74 and .github/workflows/verify.yml both state that rogue3#57 closed the exemption keyed on 'the root is not under the temp dir'. Measured at d2c4e2f it is a LIVE single-edit gate defeat: inserting 'if not (root.StartsWith(Path.GetTempPath(), StringComparison.Ordinal)) then [] else' at the head of templateDriftViolations, with real drift on disk, gives SelfTest 164 case(s), 0 failure(s), verdict pass, exit 0. The relocation #57 added moves the CURRENT DIRECTORY; that form never mentions the current directory, so nothing in the relocation reaches it.
evidence: issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#74;file:.github/workflows/verify.yml;command:./fake.sh -t SelfTest on a git-archive export of d2c4e2f carrying that one line plus drift appended to .agents/skills/fs-gg-ai/SKILL.md (exit 0)
cost: One re-measurement round: the first run of this mutant reported exit 1 and looked killed, because the export tree was under /tmp and Path.GetTempPath() is /tmp on this host, so the mutant's own predicate was false for it.
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 - issue authoring and .github/workflows/verify.yml; a mutation-survivor claim should name the mutant's exact text and the tree it was measured on.

summary: A mutation harness that exports the tree under /tmp silently confounds every mutant whose predicate mentions Path.GetTempPath(). TMPDIR is unset on this host so GetTempPath() is /tmp, and the scratchpad the worker is told to use is under /tmp, so an export placed there satisfies 'root is under the temp dir' and a mutant keyed on its negation reads as killed when it is live.
evidence: command:./fake.sh -t SelfTest on the same mutant in two locations - under /tmp (exit 1, reads as killed) and under $HOME/.cache (exit 0, live defeat)
cost: One full re-measurement of the mutant set after relocating the harness.
owner: FS-GG/fs-gg-testing - guidance for mutation harnesses over build.fsx: place the export outside every directory a mutant predicate can name, and state where it was placed alongside the result.

summary: A self-checking gate cannot be bound to its subject by a better fingerprint; it is bound by a POSITIVE CONTROL that makes the real subject fail. Planting a real violation in the real repository and requiring the real check to report it kills every exemption keyed on what the root contains or is called, in one construct, because the tree under test IS the repository. Measured: five repository-fingerprint mutants that all exit 0 at d2c4e2f (Rogue3.slnx present, build.fsx present, src/ present, .gitignore present, root not under temp) all exit 1 after, and they exit 1 on a CLEAN tree too - the exemption itself is now the failure, not merely the drift it would have hidden.
evidence: command:./fake.sh -t SelfTest over 16 mutant trees exported outside /tmp (5 fingerprint mutants x drifted and clean, 3 probe-aware, 1 plant-structure, 5 defence-disarming, 2 controls);file:build.fsx
owner: FS-GG/fs-gg-testing - this is a reusable pattern for any self-verifying checker: assert the NEGATIVE control (clean tree reports nothing) and the POSITIVE control (a violation planted in the real subject is reported), because the negative control alone is what a check that stopped looking also produces.

summary: A probe that announces itself becomes the next fingerprint, and the announcement can be anything - a literal OR a structure. The first version of this fix appended a self-describing marker comment so a killed run left something legible; one line scanning the kit tree for that marker was a live single-edit defeat (exit 0, verdict pass, real drift on disk). Replacing the marker with 'append the file to itself' removed the literal and left a STRUCTURE, and 'this file is its own bytes twice' is one line and a defeat in turn. Only an arbitrary plant - 16 GUID bytes, a bare-GUID directory name - leaves nothing to recognise.
evidence: command:./fake.sh -t SelfTest with the exemption 'File.Exists Rogue3.slnx && not (any kit file contains the marker)' - exit 0 against the marker version, exit 1 against the arbitrary-plant version;command:./fake.sh -t SelfTest with the exemption 'File.Exists Rogue3.slnx && not (the probed file is its own bytes twice)' - exit 1 against the arbitrary-plant version;file:build.fsx
cost: Two implementation rounds and two full re-measurements of the probe-aware mutant set; both were found by writing the attacking mutant rather than by review.
owner: FS-GG/fs-gg-testing - a fault-injection probe's plant must be indistinguishable in kind from the fault it simulates, or the probe's own signature becomes the exemption predicate. Worth stating as a rule wherever self-test fault injection is described.
